brief.headline: Target ₹0.65–0.80/pc for 28 mm caps (market has headroom at higher volume) and qualify Manjushree or Mold-Tek as a second source — Empire publishes no financials so lean on market benchmarks and backups to drive the ask

priceAsk.summary: Push price down to ₹0.65–0.80/pc range for 28 mm induction-wad PP caps at higher volume or looser spec
priceAsk.basis: Market ask for 28 mm caps is ₹0.55–1.20/pc (typical ₹0.85–0.95); verdict says 'MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec' — so our target sits at the lower end of that headroom band

paymentTermAsk.summary: Hold at 30 days after receipt — no reason to extend given we have no data on their cash needs and our terms aren't the worst

brief.financialLeverage: Empire publishes no financials so we cannot see how healthy or cash-tight they are. Our ₹67.47 L annual spend is meaningful but we lack the numbers to know if we're a big fish to them. That means we build our case on market data and credible alternates — not on squeezing a supplier we can't see inside. Line up a second source (Manjushree or Mold-Tek) to show we have options, then negotiate the price ask off the market benchmark where there is modest headroom at volume.

evidence.point: Market benchmark for 28 mm induction-wad PP caps shows headroom to ₹0.65–0.80/pc at higher volume or looser spec
Typical market ask for this cap is ₹0.85–0.95/pc, so our target is below that range
We spend ₹67.47 L a year with Empire on rigid plastic packaging
We already pay after 30 days of receipt — not the worst terms in our book
Manjushree Technopack is India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter with revenue of ₹2569.83 Cr — a strong second-source candidate for pharma bottles and caps

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; top second-source candidate

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹946.50 Cr revenue, health B 73/100) doing pails, containers, pharma — robust alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: IVL Dhunseri Petrochem Industries Private Limited
alternates.why: A lead to qualify (verify before RFQ) — manufacturer in India-East, medium confidence

risks: Empire publishes no financials so we fly blind on their health and cash position — if they are fragile we won't see it coming
We have no internal price comparison (no bestPriceWePay) so the negotiation leans entirely on the market ask — make sure the spec and volume match that benchmark
Market backups (Reliance, IVL Dhunseri, others) are leads only — not qualified or priced yet; do not treat them as approved alternates in the room
If we push too hard without a qualified second source in place, Empire may walk and we have no immediate fallback
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to talk about bringing our 28 mm cap price down toward ₹0.65–0.80 per piece at higher volume — the market shows headroom there — and also about qualifying a second supplier so we have backup capacity.
